lines.text: Today you will learn how to make your sprites react when you press a key or click.
An event is something that happens.
Pressing a key is an event. Clicking a sprite is an event.
Clicking the green flag is an event too.
Event blocks are called hat blocks, because they sit on top of a script like a hat.
Each script waits until its event happens, then it runs.
One sprite can have lots of scripts, each with its own hat.
A script without a hat block never starts by itself.
Put a hat on top, and the script knows when to run.
Let us make a sprite move with the arrow keys.
Change x by 10 moves right. Change x by minus 10 moves left.
For up and down, use change y.
Brilliant! Now build arrow-key controls in Scratch, then solve the puzzles.
